findings.title: is_shared_with id guard precedes global check
findings.problem: The new `if not self.id: return False` runs before the is_global and project-shared branches, so an id-less global or project-shared assistant that previously returned True now returns False.
findings.impact: Behavior regression outside the named-grant feature for unsaved assistants; whether a live caller reaches it with an id-less object was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Move the id guard below the is_global and project-shared checks, directly before the per-user grant DB lookup.

findings.title: Assistant delete commits grant removal before assistant row
findings.problem: AssistantShareService.remove_all_grants commits the grant deletes and audit rows in its own session, then assistant.delete() runs separately. If assistant.delete() (or later work) fails, the grants are gone and audited as removed while the assistant remains. Tests mock the session and assistant.delete and never fail the delete.
findings.impact: Recipients silently lose access to a still-existing assistant, and the audit trail shows removals for it.
findings.recommendation: Delete grants, audit rows and the assistant row in one transaction (or pass the session through) so a failing delete rolls grant removal back, keeping audit failure aborting the delete; add a test where assistant.delete raises.

findings.title: Optional[Select] return annotation
findings.problem: Permission.named_grant_resource_ids is annotated Optional[Select]; code-quality.md prefers `X | None` over typing.Optional.
findings.impact: Documented code-quality standard broken in new code.
findings.recommendation: Change the return annotation to `Select | None`.

findings.title: Named-grant predicate lacks effective tests
findings.problem: The predicate (resource_type, principal_type, principal_id) is only checked by SQL-substring assertions or with the session mocked, so a flipped comparison or a dropped principal_type filter would pass every test. The current code reads correct.
findings.impact: A regression in this security-critical predicate would expose other users' privately shared assistants in lists and READ checks with all tests green.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that compiles Permission.named_grant_resource_ids(user) and asserts bound params and `=` operators, or runs it against a real/sqlite session with grants for two users and asserts only the caller's ids return.

findings.title: Bare list in response models
findings.problem: SharedWithResponse.shared_with and SharableUsersResponse.users are annotated with bare `list`; code-quality.md forbids bare list/dict annotations and the OpenAPI schema loses item typing.
findings.impact: Documented standard broken in new code; response schema says nothing about the user dict shape.
findings.recommendation: Declare `list[dict[str, str | None]]` or a small item model for both fields.

findings.title: Omitted q bypasses sharable-users min length
findings.problem: `q: str = Query(default="", min_length=2)` does not validate the default, so GET /assistants/{id}/sharable-users without q reaches search_sharable_users with search=None and returns up to 20 internal directory users. Story AC and spec require short queries to be rejected (or return no users); only q=b is tested.
findings.impact: A required story criterion is only partially met; any assistant owner can enumerate directory users without the minimum-length guard.
findings.recommendation: Make q required (`Query(..., min_length=2)`) or reject empty/short values in the service; add a test for the omitted-q case.

findings.title: Share service lacks future import and annotations
findings.problem: New module has no `from __future__ import annotations`, leaves assistant/assistant_like parameters unannotated on grant, revoke, list_for_owner, search_sharable_users_for_owner and assistant_uses_personal_integration, and returns bare list[dict].
findings.impact: Documented code-quality standard for new code is only partly met.
findings.recommendation: Add the future import, annotate assistant as Assistant (or AssistantBase), and parameterize returns as list[dict[str, str | None]].

findings.title: Grants to deleted users invisible but still blocking
findings.problem: list_shared_with drops rows whose user get_by_id returns nothing, while has_named_grants counts every ASSISTANT row. Nothing purges grants when a user is deleted or deactivated. Whether get_by_id filters deleted users was not confirmed.
findings.impact: A stale grant blocks adding personal integrations on update but is invisible in shared-with, so the owner cannot see what to revoke.
findings.recommendation: Surface orphan grants in the list (or purge them on user deletion/deactivation) so has_named_grants and shared-with agree.

findings.title: Generic permission create accepts assistant resources
findings.problem: ResourceType.ASSISTANT now resolves in _lookup, so POST /permissions with resource_type=assistant and principal_type=application passes _check_ability and _check_principal and saves a row with no audit event and none of the share service's checks. The delete path was moved to the share service but create was not, and no test covers it.
findings.impact: Unaudited ASSISTANT rows can be created by an owner or admin; they inflate has_named_grants and block updates carrying personal integrations.
findings.recommendation: Reject ResourceType.ASSISTANT in PermissionCreationService.run (raise PermissionAccessDenied), or route it through AssistantShareService with an audit event; add a test.

findings.title: Commit subject violates ticket-prefix format
findings.problem: git-workflow.md requires 'EPMCDME-####: Description'; the subject 'epmcdme-14786: add planning artifacts' uses a lowercase ticket prefix and description.
findings.impact: Breaks ticket-prefix tooling and history conventions; documented blocking commit-format standard.
findings.recommendation: Reword the commit to 'EPMCDME-14786: Add planning artifacts' or ensure the squash subject conforms.
